//: `@/*` resolves against the mobile root FIRST and ../src second, and a
path list applies to every file in the program — including the web
modules pulled in through @shared/. So a mobile module sitting at a
path some web module imports as `@/<path>` silently shadows the web
one for that import. mobile/lib/languages.ts did this to
src/lib/languages.ts: the WhatsApp templates resolved to the trimmed
mobile mirror and failed on exports it does not carry, and because
the mobile job only runs on mobile/** changes, main stayed green
until an unrelated mobile PR surfaced it.
The rule this alias needs is therefore: the two roots must not
overlap. No file under mobile/ may sit at a path that also exists
under src/. Both sides assert it — mobile/lib/alias-shadowing.test.ts
and the same case in src/lib/mobile-parity.test.ts — because each CI
job only sees its own half of the diff.
